html:
The Wunambal are an Aboriginal Australian people of the far north Kimberley coast of Western Australia, around the Mitchell Plateau and Admiralty Gulf. The map shows them as Wunambul from 1600 to 1815.

With their neighbours the Worrorra and Ngarinyin, they share the law of the Wandjina, the rain and creator beings painted in rock shelters across their country. The region is also home to the older Gwion Gwion paintings. Their neighbours to the east were the Gambera. Their rugged country stayed largely free of settlers, and in 2011 the Wunambal Gaambera people had their native title recognised over much of it.
